**M3. CONTROLLER AND MONITORING**

The CryoStore 3000 is fitted with the CryoCare CS-3000 controller, which provides the
following functions:

According to the specification sheet, the CryoStore 3000 capacity_liters is 350. Record status: current.

- Temperature display (PT100 sensor, 4-wire).
- Liquid level display (capacitance probe), shown as percentage of full capacity.
- High/low temperature alarms (user-adjustable, default setpoints: -190°C low,
  -170°C high).
- Low level alarm (default setpoint: 15%).
- Auto-fill control: solenoid valve opens when level drops below setpoint (default
  20%) and closes at 25%. The auto-fill function is enabled via the front panel
  keypad.
- Data logging: the controller stores the last 90 days of temperature and level
  readings at 15-minute intervals. Data can be downloaded via the USB port on the
  front panel.
- Audible and visual alarms (buzzer and red indicator lamp). The buzzer can be muted
  for 30 minutes; the lamp remains lit until the alarm condition is cleared.
- Remote alarm output: dry contact relay, rated 24 V DC, 1 A, connected to the
  building management system (BMS) via the alarm panel in the Cryo Suite.
- Power failure alarm: the controller detects loss of mains power and switches to
  battery backup. The buzzer sounds immediately; the display shows "POWER FAIL".

3. Root Cause

Preliminary investigation indicates a failure of the 22 kV busbar joint at the substation feeding Block 12. The joint arced and tripped the upstream circuit breaker (CB-12-E2). The cause is suspected to be thermal degradation of the joint insulation due to prolonged high loading during the recent warm weather (ambient temperatures above 33°C recorded on 2025-01-12 to 2025-01-14). A detailed thermographic survey of the substation was conducted on 2025-01-15 at 16:00; findings are attached in Appendix A.

4. Root Cause Analysis Summary (Preliminary)

The Electrical Services Team has provided a preliminary summary of the root cause. This is pending final approval in the complete report due by 2025-01-20.

- The outage was caused by a failure of the insulation boot on a busbar joint on feeder E2 in the Block 12 substation.
- The failure led to a phase-to-phase fault, which was cleared by the upstream protective device.
- The joint and insulation boot have been replaced (as detailed in the original report).
- A thermographic survey of the repaired joint and adjacent feeders was conducted on 2025-01-15 and showed no anomalies.
- A follow-up thermographic survey is scheduled for 2025-01-29 to monitor the repaired joint.

5. Actions Taken Since Original Report

The Power Outage Report 2025-01-15 states the outage_duration_minutes as 47. Record status: historical.

- 2025-01-16, 10:00: Safety briefing for lab users held in Lab 12-03-01. Attendance was recorded for all affected labs. Topics covered included emergency procedures during power loss, proper shutdown of sensitive equipment, and the location of emergency lighting and exit routes.
- 2025-01-16, 14:00: The autoclave AV-4 was taken out of service and tagged with a "Do Not Operate" sign. A work order has been raised for the validation run.
- 2025-01-17, 09:30: Electrical Services Team conducted a visual inspection of the substation and found no new issues.
- 2025-01-17, 11:00: A reminder was sent to all building occupants to ensure their personal equipment (e.g., laptops, phones) is backed up, as the UPS units are for critical shared equipment only.

6. Equipment Status Update

- Generator G2: Operational. Fuel level checked on 2025-01-16 at 08:00, topped up to 80%.
- LN2 freezer (Unit CS3000, Lab 12-04-05): LN2 level was refilled to 85% on 2025-01-15 at 16:20. A second refill was performed on 2025-01-17 at 09:00 to maintain levels during the weekend. Temperature has been logged and remains within acceptable range.
- UPS units: All reported normal operation. A scheduled load test for the UPS serving Lab 12-04 is planned for 2025-01-22 at 14:00. Please ensure no critical processes are running on that circuit during the test.

7. Follow-up Items (Updated)

- Root cause analysis report to be completed by 2025-01-20 (assigned to Electrical Services Team). This is on track.
- Review of busbar joint maintenance schedule for Block 12 substation to be completed by the end of January.
- Consideration of additional temperature sensors on busbar joints is under review by the Electrical Services Team. A cost estimate is expected by 2025-01-24.
- New item: Work order raised for autoclave AV-4 validation. Estimated completion by 2025-01-23.
- New item: Battery health check for fume hoods on Level 3 to be included in the February preventive maintenance schedule.

8. Attachments (Updated)

- Appendix A: Thermographic Survey Report (2025-01-15)
- Appendix B: Alarm Log Extract (14:30 – 15:30)
- Appendix C: Floor Plan with Affected Areas
- Appendix D: Preliminary Root Cause Analysis Summary (2025-01-17)
- Appendix E: Autoclave AV-4 Service Tag Photograph (2025-01-16)
**POWER OUTAGE REPORT – BLOCK 12**
**Incident No.:** ELEC-2025-0014
**Date of Incident:** 2025-01-15
**Report Status:** Final (Version 2.0)

---

**9. Root Cause Analysis (Final)**

The preliminary analysis circulated on 2025-01-17 has been confirmed. The incident was caused by a
single-phase-to-earth fault at the busbar joint on the outgoing circuit to Lab 12-04. The fault
current was insufficient to trip the upstream circuit breaker, resulting in sustained arcing that
degraded the joint insulation over a period of several hours.

Contributory factors identified:

- **Thermal cycling:** The busbar joint had been in service since the 2011 substation refurbishment.
  Differential expansion across the joint had gradually reduced contact pressure.
- **Inadequate torque verification:** Maintenance records indicate that the last torque check on this
  joint was performed during the 2022 preventive maintenance cycle. The specified re-torque interval
  for this joint type is 18 months.
- **Ambient temperature:** The substation room temperature on the day of the incident was logged at
  31.5°C at 14:00, which is within the design envelope but above the 28°C average for the preceding
  week. This is noted as a minor aggravating factor only.
- **No prior thermographic anomaly:** The last thermographic survey of Block 12 substation was
  conducted on 2024-11-12. No abnormal temperature rise was recorded at that time. The fault
  developed between that survey and the incident date.

The Electrical Services Team has completed its investigation. The root cause is confirmed as
insulation breakdown at the busbar joint due to loss of contact pressure, exacerbated by thermal
cycling. No design flaw in the switchgear has been identified.

**9.1 Corrective Actions Completed**

1.  **2025-01-18, 10:00:** The affected busbar joint was replaced. The new joint is of the same
    type but was installed using a calibrated torque wrench and with the application of joint
    compound. Photographs of the removed joint were taken and are attached as **Appendix F**.
2.  **2025-01-18, 14:30:** Insulation resistance testing was performed on the repaired busbar
    section. Results were within acceptable limits (all phases > 100 MΩ at 1 kV).
3.  **2025-01-19, 09:00:** The circuit to Lab 12-04 was re-energised. All equipment was
    successfully restored, with the exception of items already noted in Section 5 of this report.
4.  **2025-01-19, 11:00:** A full load test was conducted on the repaired circuit. The circuit
    carried the normal lab load for 2 hours without any abnormal readings.

**10. Recommendations**

The following recommendations are made to reduce the likelihood of a similar incident. These are
general recommendations for the campus electrical distribution system and are not limited to Block
12.

**10.1 Maintenance Schedule Review**

- **Re-torque interval:** The preventive maintenance schedule for all busbar joints in campus
  substations should be reviewed. The current interval of 18 months should be reduced to 12 months
  for joints that have been in service for more than 10 years. This change should be incorporated
  into the 2026 maintenance calendar.
- **Thermographic surveys:** The frequency of thermographic surveys for substations should be
  increased from annual to semi-annual for buildings with critical laboratory loads. The additional
  surveys should be scheduled for the months of May and November to avoid the peak holiday periods.
- **Torque verification records:** A standardised checklist for busbar joint maintenance should be
  adopted across all campus substations. The checklist should include a field for the torque value
  achieved and the serial number of the torque wrench used.

**M2. CONSTRUCTION AND MATERIALS**

  rack 3 – green, rack 4 – yellow, rack 5 – orange, rack 6 – purple.

  (see section J).

**M3. CONTROLLER AND MONITORING**

The CryoStore 3000 is fitted with the CryoCare CS-3000 controller, which provides the
following functions:

According to the specification sheet, the CryoStore 3000 capacity_liters is 350. Record status: current.

- Temperature display (PT100 sensor, 4-wire).
- Liquid level display (capacitance probe), shown as percentage of full capacity.
- High/low temperature alarms (user-adjustable, default setpoints: -190°C low,
  -170°C high).
- Low level alarm (default setpoint: 15%).
- Auto-fill control: solenoid valve opens when level drops below setpoint (default
  20%) and closes at 25%. The auto-fill function is enabled via the front panel
  keypad.
- Data logging: the controller stores the last 90 days of temperature and level
  readings at 15-minute intervals. Data can be downloaded via the USB port on the
  front panel.
- Audible and visual alarms (buzzer and red indicator lamp). The buzzer can be muted
  for 30 minutes; the lamp remains lit until the alarm condition is cleared.
- Remote alarm output: dry contact relay, rated 24 V DC, 1 A, connected to the
  building management system (BMS) via the alarm panel in the Cryo Suite.
- Power failure alarm: the controller detects loss of mains power and switches to
  battery backup. The buzzer sounds immediately; the display shows "POWER FAIL".

documents.content:
**POWER OUTAGE REPORT – BLOCK 12**
**Incident No.:** ELEC-2025-0014
**Date of Incident:** 2025-01-15
**Report Status:** Final (Version 2.0)

---

**9. Root Cause Analysis (Final)**

The preliminary analysis circulated on 2025-01-17 has been confirmed. The incident was caused by a
single-phase-to-earth fault at the busbar joint on the outgoing circuit to Lab 12-04. The fault
current was insufficient to trip the upstream circuit breaker, resulting in sustained arcing that
degraded the joint insulation over a period of several hours.

Contributory factors identified:

- **Thermal cycling:** The busbar joint had been in service since the 2011 substation refurbishment.
  Differential expansion across the joint had gradually reduced contact pressure.
- **Inadequate torque verification:** Maintenance records indicate that the last torque check on this
  joint was performed during the 2022 preventive maintenance cycle. The specified re-torque interval
  for this joint type is 18 months.
- **Ambient temperature:** The substation room temperature on the day of the incident was logged at
  31.5°C at 14:00, which is within the design envelope but above the 28°C average for the preceding
  week. This is noted as a minor aggravating factor only.
- **No prior thermographic anomaly:** The last thermographic survey of Block 12 substation was
  conducted on 2024-11-12. No abnormal temperature rise was recorded at that time. The fault
  developed between that survey and the incident date.

The Electrical Services Team has completed its investigation. The root cause is confirmed as
insulation breakdown at the busbar joint due to loss of contact pressure, exacerbated by thermal
cycling. No design flaw in the switchgear has been identified.

**9.1 Corrective Actions Completed**

1.  **2025-01-18, 10:00:** The affected busbar joint was replaced. The new joint is of the same
    type but was installed using a calibrated torque wrench and with the application of joint
    compound. Photographs of the removed joint were taken and are attached as **Appendix F**.
2.  **2025-01-18, 14:30:** Insulation resistance testing was performed on the repaired busbar
    section. Results were within acceptable limits (all phases > 100 MΩ at 1 kV).
3.  **2025-01-19, 09:00:** The circuit to Lab 12-04 was re-energised. All equipment was
    successfully restored, with the exception of items already noted in Section 5 of this report.
4.  **2025-01-19, 11:00:** A full load test was conducted on the repaired circuit. The circuit
    carried the normal lab load for 2 hours without any abnormal readings.

**10. Recommendations**

The following recommendations are made to reduce the likelihood of a similar incident. These are
general recommendations for the campus electrical distribution system and are not limited to Block
12.

**10.1 Maintenance Schedule Review**

- **Re-torque interval:** The preventive maintenance schedule for all busbar joints in campus
  substations should be reviewed. The current interval of 18 months should be reduced to 12 months
  for joints that have been in service for more than 10 years. This change should be incorporated
  into the 2026 maintenance calendar.
- **Thermographic surveys:** The frequency of thermographic surveys for substations should be
  increased from annual to semi-annual for buildings with critical laboratory loads. The additional
  surveys should be scheduled for the months of May and November to avoid the peak holiday periods.
- **Torque verification records:** A standardised checklist for busbar joint maintenance should be
  adopted across all campus substations. The checklist should include a field for the torque value
  achieved and the serial number of the torque wrench used.
